raw_segments.text: First period, in 1350, and for some time before, the average price of the quarter of wheat
in England seems not to have been estimated lower than four ounces of silver tower weight,
equal to about twenty shillings of our present money.
From this price it seems to have fallen gradually to two ounces of silver, equal to about ten
shillings of our present money, the price at which we find it estimated in the beginning
of the sixteenth century, and at which it seems to have continued to be estimated till
